previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and cardiomyopathy was admitted for acute shortness of breath and orthopnea. She had progressive dyspnea over a week, a mild cough, and was unable to lie flat. Initial evaluation revealed moderate pulmonary edema on chest X-ray and elevated blood pressure. She was treated with BiPAP, nitroglycerin drip, and underwent hemodialysis with removal of 2.3 liters of fluid, leading to significant improvement in respiratory status. A repeat X-ray showed reduced opacities, though a retrocardiac infiltrate raised concern for possible pneumonia, prompting a course of levofloxacin. Echocardiogram confirmed severe diastolic dysfunction and moderate pulmonary hypertension, unchanged from prior. Her blood pressure stabilized, allowing discontinuation of the nitro drip and resumption of oral antihypertensives. She was discharged home breathing room air, with instructions to restrict fluids, continue antibiotics, and hold cinacalcet until after her next dialysis session.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o female with history of HTN, CM with EF 60-65%, SLE with 
renal failure, on HD, presenting with intermittent SSCP with 
hyperacute T waves and negative cardiac enzymes.  
.  
# Chest pain: Ddx is broad.  Must not miss etiologies would 
mainly include ACS/Unstable angina.  Highest on differential is 
musculoskeletal cause. PE or pericarditis is also on 
differential.  PE seemed very unlikely given that her CP is not 
pleuritic, there is no hypoxia on VS, and also no right heart 
strain on EKG.  Pericarditis is a possibility given her lupus, 
however no changes on EKG show signs of pericarditis, such as PR 
depression or ST elevation.  Also, CP is positional, however not 
classic for pericarditis (pain worsens when leaning forward).
.
Of note, ACS/Unstable angina was ruled out with cardiac enzymes 
times three.  Nonetheless, she was started on full dose aspirin, 
atorva 80, and maintained on her HTN regimen while here.  We 
d/c'ed her ASA and atorva at time of discharge given that she 
has had elevated LFTs in the past and is followed by cardiology.
.
MSK is the most likely cause given the reproducibility on exam.  
We maintained the pt on her home dilaudid PO regimen which was 
helpful.  We avoided any NSAIDs given her ESRD.  She does 
endorse picking up some heavy groceries prior to the CP, however 
cannot recall any other trauma or heavy lifting.  Most episodes 
subsided without intervention except for the first one.  of 
note, pt endorses recent dx of rotator cuff tear in left 
shoulder where pain also is located and states already has ortho 
f/u.
